A state of discomfort arising from bashfulness or consciousness of having violated a social rule; humiliation.

examples.text: The desired effect [of affectionate teasing] is a look of pleasurable embarrassment, as if you administered a compliment. Anyone who doesn't stop teasing immediately upon producing real embarrassment, anger or tears is not really teasing.

glosses: A person or thing which is the cause of humiliation to another.

examples.text: Jack, you are an embarrassment to this family.

The audacious hijacking in Paris of a van carrying the baggage of a Saudi prince to his private jet is obviously an embarrassment to the French capital, whose ultra-high-end boutiques have suffered a spate of heists in recent months.

glosses: A large collection of good or valuable things, especially one that exceeds requirements or causes some sort of hindrance.

examples.text: There are over 5,000 Americans now in Paris, many artists, singers, musicians, writers, and actors, so many, indeed, the committee could hardly pick a program from an embarrassment of volunteers.
